contract.json_path: select_all -> /selection/select_all, unique_test_case_count -> /selection/unique_test_case_count, folders -> /selection/folders. These describe how the backend nests the body internally, NOT the shape the MCP invoke surface accepts: sending a literal 'selection' wrapper object is rejected ('unknown body: selection...'). The invoke surface wants select_all, folders, show, q, count, p, shared_selection, unique_test_case_count all as FLAT top-level body keys. Guidance also calls 'selection' (i.e. select_all/folders together) 'effectively mandatory', but neither is schema-marked required — only project_id (path) is.

notes:
TOP-LEVEL CONTRACT IS CORRECT. success/info/test_cases/selected are all present exactly as declared, with no envelope wrapper — matches guidance point 'The response is flat — {success, info, test_cases, selected}'. selected=null in default (filtered) mode and an array in show='all' mode, exactly as guidance point 4 describes. The DRIFT is entirely inside test_cases[]: the declared item schema (rich nested objects for assignee/creator_details/case_type/priority/status, plus tags/issues/custom_fields/steps/links/comments_count/history_count) describes essentially a DIFFERENT, richer 'test case detail' object than what this endpoint actually returns. The real item is a flat record with different field names entirely (folder_id not test_case_folder_id, automation_status as a bare string not an object, no priority/status/case_type sub-objects, no tags/issues/custom_fields at all). Given the size of the mismatch, this reads like the response schema was copied from a different (detail-view) test-case endpoint rather than authored against this selection endpoint's actual serializer.

COUNT-VS-ROWS: CLEAN across every call made — info.count always equalled len(test_cases): 2/2 (folder 764093), 18/18 (folder 764138 alone), 19/19 (764138 + subfolder 764828 named explicitly), 21/21 (project-wide select_all). No desync found here, unlike the four other capabilities flagged this session.

RECURSION IS UNDOCUMENTED AND OFF BY DEFAULT: selecting folder 764138 with test_case_select_all=true returns only its 18 DIRECT cases. The 19th (recursive) case lives in subfolder 764828 and is only included once 764828 is added as its own key in the `folders` map (confirmed: {764138:{...}, 764828:{...}} => count 19). Nothing in the guidance or schema states that folder selection is non-recursive, or that a caller must enumerate every subfolder id itself to preview what a recursive run-create would actually pull in — a real risk for an agent that trusts 'test_case_select_all' to mean 'the whole subtree'.

ISSUE FILTER: NOT SUPPORTED. Passing q={'issue_ids':[999999]} (a bogus id) against a project-wide select_all returned the full, unfiltered 21-case set with no error (attempt 7) — the key was silently ignored rather than rejected or applied. Separately, q={'search':'probe case A'} against the 2-case readonly folder with show='all' returned BOTH cases as members of `selected` (attempt 6), i.e. it did not narrow to the one case whose name actually matches — suggesting 'search' isn't the recognized free-text key either, or filtering silently no-ops for unrecognized q shapes. The `q` param is declared only as {type:object} with no property schema (an unfalsifiable declaration per this session's running list), and guidance's plain-English gloss ('a search string... matched against case name and identifier') never says what key that string goes under. Net: this capability cannot answer 'which cases would this ticket pull in' — confirming, from this side too, that the routing eval was right to reject count_run_selection for the same query. Neither the count- nor list-producing member of this pair takes an issue/ticket filter.

count_run_selection_v1 PAIRING: NOT a documented pair, matching the pattern this session is tracking. The only cross-reference is one-way and narrow: list_test_runs_selection's own `shared_selection` field description says 'Accepted by the parameter filter but NOT read by this action — cases shared in from other projects are not resolved here. Use the count endpoint if you need shared selections accounted for' — it never names count_run_selection explicitly, and it's scoped to the shared_selection edge case only, not framed as a general preview-then-list workflow. Cross-checked against tests/live/runs/tm/count_run_selection.json from this same session: its guidance contains ZERO mention of list_test_runs_selection or any list/preview capability at all. So unlike the archived-plans and binned-cases pairs (which reportedly cross-reference each other explicitly, both directions), this is another unlabelled near-duplicate: same selection input shape (select_all/folders/shared_selection), overlapping purpose (count_run_selection returns {success,count}; this one returns the actual rows plus its own info.count), but no real documented pairing for a routing agent to discover from either side.

ERROR ENVELOPE: attempt 1's failure never reached the live TM API — it was caught by the MCP invoke surface's own parameter guard, which returns a flat {ok:false, error:'<string>'} shape, structurally different from the declared 400/401/404/500 API error schema ({success:false, error:{code, message, details}}). No genuine live 4xx/5xx was triggered in this probe (every real API call returned 200), so declared-vs-actual error-envelope drift could not be checked here one way or the other — flagging the transport-vs-API distinction only, not diffing an error body against the success schema.
